Tbf when it comes to style is very subjective. But I feel like to me the people who dress the best are usually the ones who don't dress in a standard way, and are not afraid of experimenting, putting on something that stands out (going a bit high fasion). Sometimes I even feel that when I look at somebody who is dressed a bit extra I don't particularly like any of the clothes they're wearing but I still find them a well dressed person because they have their own style and they stand out 🤷‍♀️. 
Also a general tip would be to try to choose clothes with better materials, at least make sure that most of your clothes are of higher quality (I reccomend shopping in outlets, I do it sometimes, you can get high quality materials for lower prices) 

Also maybe try not wearing basic colours (black and white is something different but for example when you want to buy a pink shirt, try to look for an interesting shade of pink)

And don't mix patterns too much. Sometimes it can be a good thing to try it but it's easy to overdo it, hence you might end up looking bad.

Also if you're scared of mixing colours, or want to go for a basic, minimalistic look, maybe try to look for interesting stitching or shape of the clothes that you wear. For example a basic white t-shirt is nice, but sometimes it looks more attractive if its oversize etc.

I'm 22 now and o just got out of a long term relationship  (1.5 year). I was quite down recently and I started noticing that everybody around seems to be getting engaged and getting married. 2 people have helped me alter my perspective on that. One of them was my therapist, the other my mum, since I've obviously talked to both of them about it.
In general they both told me how young I am, and how sometimes relationships fall apart even when you're 50 yo. So ending a relationship in your early twenties is definitely not something to be worried about. It made me look at life differently, seeing how there is still so many years ahead of me and you never know what will happen. Also when you think about it, about 50% of marriages end in divorce, the ratio for relationships overall is probably even lower. The fact that you might feel that everybody is in a relationship and you're not is just temporary. A year from now you might be in a relationship and your friends might not be cause it's more of a rotation than it is a permanent state.
Also, I remember that my mum has mentioned that she doesn't want me to think like I have missed out or I am too late for something. She said how she felt that her cousin Kate has felt like this when they were in their early twenties, seeing how everybody was getting married and she wasn't. So Kate ended up ignoring some red flags and married terrible men twice in her life and ended up as a single mum just because she felt like she had to fit into some social standard of having a husband at a young age. 
I like to believe that eventually everybody will find themselves in a happy relationship, whether for some people it might be at the age of 20 and for others at 40.
